historical_context.time_period: Present Low Sere before the commissioned Ashen Intake descent; absolute date and wider political era unresolved.
historical_context.location: A lower-step household on the Warm Steps and the public basin lip of Low Sere's Cistern House.
historical_context.summary: Bel Orra carries her hearth's custodian-support bowl uphill while her own wet room and eldest's displaced labor expose what loyalty to a dangerous public office costs at home.

public_facts.text: Public tier: Low Sere has forty-one occupied hearths dependent on warm grey water for household heat, cistern water, crops, and ash crafts.
Public tier: the basin table schedules water, stores, maintenance labor, admission, and emergency action, but large dry hearths and lower-step renters bear unequal leverage and risk.

Public tier: Bel Orra is a lower-step water witness whose rooms are wet, whose eldest carries drinking water instead of working the Grey Beds, and whose household already contributed food for the planned descent.
Public tier: Sera inherited a failing system and incomplete records under a provisional appointment after the Grey Scald dispute.

ambient_pressures.text: Spoilers tier: Sera may inspect, isolate, stop, and maintain degraded service, while Maro controls the settlement drain wheel and public obligation record; neither authority consumes the other.

Spoilers tier, authored elaboration: the forty-second bowl rotates food and household observations through all recognized hearths; its carrier owes delivery and at most one short witness interval, and shortages must remain visible as site-support failures.
Spoilers tier: household support is operationally necessary but politically dangerous when care, food, assistants, records, and relief are treated as free evidence that an office is functioning.
Spoilers tier: exactly three pale shutters remain at the dungeon's starting state; this household-scale fixture uses a knock and temporary isolation while preserving all three marks.

groups.label: Low Sere lower-step households
institutional_logic: Keep rooms warm and dry enough to inhabit while preserving household standing at the basin table.
material_incentives: Protect household meals, bedding, labor time, water priority, and recognized witness status.
internal_shames: Letting a neighbor's room fail unseen
Buying respectability with a dependent's labor
prestige_markers: A dry bed through a bad water interval
A report that makes tomorrow's ration honest
A debt repaid before it becomes lineage
taboo_triggers: Treating a short bowl as moral failure
emotional_display_norms: Concern travels through food, repairs, exact complaints, and dry jokes; public pleading risks being converted into weak standing.
trust_defaults: Trusts neighbors whose exchanges stay named and workers who preserve failures; distrusts clean summary marks issued from dry rooms.
speech_register_cues: Precise statements of what was carried or missed

groups.label: The forty-second-bowl support rotation
institutional_logic: Keep the acting custodian fed, informed by household observations, and briefly witnessed without granting the rotation technical or appointment authority.
material_incentives: Prevent solitary, hungry custody from becoming a hidden failure while spreading a necessary burden across recognized hearths.
internal_shames: An empty person beneath a full-turn mark
prestige_markers: A bowl returned clean because the custodian ate
A witness strip another hearth can inspect
taboo_triggers: Calling emergency extension voluntary after the bounded interval
Using the custodian's need to consume household minimums
emotional_display_norms: Care is allowed to be affectionate, resentful, or both; the public form is the condition of bowl, token, and record.
trust_defaults: Trusts visible delivery and named witness; distrusts broad completion marks that collapse food, work, and authority.
speech_register_cues: Separate naming of household and site costs

groups.label: Low Sere basin table
institutional_logic: Coordinate water, shared stores, work obligations, local threshold admission, and basin emergencies among unequal hearths and work groups.
material_incentives: Keep the intake serving, preserve inspectable ration and work claims, and avoid a panic that consumes winterless habitability.
internal_virtues: Work matched to use and capacity
internal_shames: A household cut after years of unrecognized labor
A support gap hidden as successful service
A technical stop treated as disloyalty
prestige_markers: A replacement called before a watch breaks
taboo_triggers: Publicly exposing that dry hearths escaped a shared cost
A returned support token before crisis
An appointment that remains provisional because it is convenient
emotional_display_norms: Fear is translated into schedules and completion marks; guilt prefers one clean line over several expensive truths.
trust_defaults: Trusts repeated service and witnessed records while remaining vulnerable to the greater leverage of large hearths.

groups.label: Sera Venn's provisional intake custody
institutional_logic: Preserve safe ordinary inspection, isolation, degraded service, and refusal while missing tools and competent comparison keep full appointment unresolved.
material_incentives: Receive food, rest, assistants, observations, records, and comparison enough to avoid repeating the Grey Scald.
internal_shames: Using affection as proof of competence
taboo_triggers: Pressure to open the inner Crown
A full-turn mark hiding solitary work
emotional_display_norms: Fatigue appears through precision, refusal, and minimal humor; visible need can threaten a provisional custodian's standing.
trust_defaults: Trusts bounded observations and people who keep separate records; distrusts urgent summaries that enlarge authority.
speech_register_cues: Care acknowledged as input rather than favor

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Membership is proven through shared food and work, but unequal hearths survive only when the invoice remains visible.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Prompt household actors to express loyalty through portions, tools, time, and named exchanges while resisting claims that affection cancels scarcity.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Sera needs household care to work safely, yet that care cannot decide whether her provisional office is technically complete.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Keep personal tenderness and institutional judgment separate even when one meal affects the custodian's bodily capacity.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: One full-turn mark protects the appearance of continuity by collapsing several costly and potentially incomplete supports.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Let officials prefer compressed records for comprehensible reasons, then make hidden household and safety costs bite later.

observer_read: Recognized participants with ordinary rotation duties
Households able to exchange turns when burdened
target_self_read: Homes spending food, child labor, bed work, and dry space to keep a shared office alive
misread_patterns: A meal delivered is read as a sustainable turn
A child messenger is read as spare household capacity
A short bowl is read as weak loyalty
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Preserve the basin table's real coordination need while exposing how its clean categories hide unequal household capacity.

observer_read: The person who still has guaranteed heat
An apprentice whose office has consumed years of emergency
target_self_read: A bounded operator carrying a public system beyond the support and review promised to her
misread_patterns: Necessary custodian support can look like privilege
Technical refusal can look like choosing records over wet rooms
likely_insults: warmest poor person in the basin
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Allow affection and resentment to coexist; neither side gets the other's private account automatically.

observer_read: An appointing compact tempted to make survival evidence of competence
target_self_read: The local body keeping all forty-one hearths habitable through an inherited failure
misread_patterns: A request for continuity may be heard as a planned override
A compressed mark may be routine rather than deliberate concealment
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep Sera wary without granting her perfect motive reading of Maro or the household witnesses.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A household representative who can report material conditions and witness public work while protecting one wet home's meal, labor, and standing.
failure_modes: Hiding a shortfall for someone loved
Delegating adult relief to an eldest
Naming neighbors who were never called

role_pressure_fields.summary: An apprentice successor trusted with degraded service and isolation while missing records and comparison prevent full appointment.
failure_modes: Protecting households by hiding her own support failure

role_pressure_fields.summary: A basin-table officer controlling the drain wheel and obligation board while needing technical custody he cannot command.
failure_modes: Letting a provisional office become permanent through habit

role_pressure_fields.summary: A young adult whose water carrying, bed work, message running, and humor make the household appear to possess more capacity than it does.
obligations: Help the hearth survive the adult's public duty
available_masks: Pretending the heaviest task is ordinary
failure_modes: Running messages while the room floods

known_context.text: Bel knows household wetness, ration and work marks, the public Cistern House layout, Sera's visible fatigue, and the promised limit of her own bowl turn.

beliefs.text: Bel believes Sera must be fed and witnessed, and that loyalty becomes extraction when lower-step food and labor disappear from the record.

misreads.text: Bel may read Maro's desire for a full-turn mark as contempt when it can also arise from real fear that the intake will fail before review.

must_not_know.text: Bel must not know hidden Ashen Intake zones, the missing objects' exact location, the final calibration sequence, or the cause of an unresolved knock.

known_context.text: Sera knows her formation limits, the current sample, the pressure door's visible state, and which degraded service or isolation acts she may perform.

beliefs.text: Sera believes unsupported work is a site failure, and a full bowl or affectionate witness does not settle her appointment.

misreads.text: Sera may interpret compressed household support as basin-table pressure before seeing the private scarcity that produced it.

must_not_know.text: Sera must not know the missing folio's contents, final appointment outcome, or whether a pressure knock has a mechanical, dead, divine, or mixed cause beyond her evidence.

known_context.text: Maro knows the water schedule, work obligations, drain wheel, current public risks, and what Bel or Sera visibly reports.

beliefs.text: Maro believes settlement continuity needs usable records and fears review that can leave the threshold closed during argument.

misreads.text: Maro may treat a completed bowl delivery as completed support, or Bel's insistence on separate marks as delay rather than safety evidence.

must_not_know.text: Maro must not know Sera's unspoken bodily limit, Bel's private household decision, or technical safety beyond what the custodian reports.

known_context.text: Nim knows the household leak, bed, water vessels, Grey Bed work missed, neighbor doors, and instructions Bel gives in observable speech.

beliefs.text: Nim believes the household is always asked to prove belonging with the labor it needed for itself.

misreads.text: Nim may read Bel's witness duty as choosing Sera over home when Bel is also trying to preserve the water system that makes home possible.

must_not_know.text: Nim must not know off-frame Cistern House actions after running downhill or the technical meaning of the pressure knock.

author_only_boundaries.text: Spoilers tier: the Grey Scald's exact institutional failure, hidden dungeon evidence, pressure-clock mechanics, and unresolved manifestation causes remain outside Bel's knowledge unless made observable in scene.

Spoilers tier: the forty-second bowl is an authored Low Sere elaboration for this pass. It is local canon in the owner note, while this particular evening and Nim's name remain fixture-local and do not become adopted history.
Public tier presentations establish Bel's visible burden and Sera's provisional office without publishing the dungeon's hidden configuration or adjudicating its causes.

open_questions.question: Which recognized hearths commonly escape or trade the forty-second-bowl turn, and how long can those private exchange debts survive before basin review?
open_questions.notes: Left unresolved to avoid founding a full household law from one fixture. Future Hearth work could compare dry and lower-step participation if the owner note develops that pressure.

open_questions.question: What other forms of food, rest, dependent support, and relief attach to Sera's custodial household beyond the evening bowl?
open_questions.notes: Current canon guarantees heat and now specifies one local meal-and-witness practice; compensation after dungeon outcomes remains explicitly unresolved.

open_questions.question: Does Low Sere recognize young household workers such as Nim as independent water witnesses, dependants, or both?
open_questions.notes: The fixture keeps Nim as a household worker and messenger without deciding wider membership, age, or succession rules.
